articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like shape-related words than the real category.
Point pushed me in that direction immediately.
Tangent kept that theory alive for a moment, but polygon still did not quite fit.
That was the moment the first idea stopped working.
Then Polygon made me stop thinking about shape-related words and start thinking about the real category.
Point fit once I read it through the answer.
Tangent fit once I read it through the answer.
Perimeter and Polygon then felt less surprising and more like the last pieces falling into place.
Looking back, the answer feels obvious in the best way.
solutionNarrative: I first read Point and Tangent too literally and drifted toward shape-related words. Point could be read as "point", while Tangent could be read as "tangent", so the board still felt open instead of solved.

Polygon changed the direction because "polygon" gave me a testable phrase, not just a loose topic. Once that line worked, I had a fixed place to put the repeated word and could go back through the earlier clues with a clearer target.

I then checked "point", "tangent", "plane", and "perimeter". Those checks mattered because each one landed as ordinary wording on its own, so I was not forcing five separate hints into one bag. The board started to behave like one phrase pattern across Point, Tangent, Plane, Perimeter, and Polygon.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Geometry terms", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
